findings.detail: Within each Skill, tickets are chronologically split into four equal parts; the first three are development data used by synthesis/simulation/attribution/revision, while the fourth is held out, fed into no stage of the loop, and used solely for measurement/reporting. All reported TSR values are on this evaluation set; version selection uses only development data.
Table 2 reports SkillEvo TSR 59.4, 71.3, 77.9, 81.8 for R1-R4; Single-turn QA 58.9, 64.5, 65.7, 66.4; Self-Reflection 59.2, 58.7, 57.4, 58.8.

Table 3 gives Full 81.8, Single-turn QA 66.4, and w/o Governance 78.6. Table 6 gives cumulative bloat +2.8% with governance versus +16.2% without governance. Table 5 gives Full-system RegR 28.2%, 24.4%, 21.1% across successive transitions and a first-to-last change of -7.1 points. The -7.1 value is a temporal change within the reported governed sequence, not a controlled governance-vs-no-governance RegR difference; the paper provides no no-governance RegR row in Table 5.

The paper separates simulator-side coverage/fidelity from agent-side exposed-intent accuracy and excludes low-coverage samples from the agent denominator. Implementation assigns the Skill Editor/Generator to deepseek-v4-pro and Verifier, User Agent, Attributor, and Governor together to minimax-m3, satisfying only the stated Generator != Evaluator family constraint. The simulator and verifier are not independently model-separated in the reported implementation; 'orthogonal' denotes responsibility/metric separation, not distinct model families for User Agent versus Verifier.

The Ethics Statement says no revision reaches production without human confirmation and calls this human checkpoint a necessary condition; Appendix G likewise places human confirmation before production rollout. Therefore the reported production method contains a residual manual-human execution gate and cannot count as a solved zero-user-execution Phase-1 route.

The reported system executes deepseek-v4-pro and minimax-m3 inference over a production ticket pipeline and requires human confirmation before rollout. It is not demonstrated to operate with optional external/model quotas at zero, and the confidential production dataset is not released. These facts do not invalidate the paper's empirical claims; they prevent promotion of the reported mechanism itself to the current zero-Work/zero-finite-quota/zero-cost acceptance path.

scope_guard: No claim is made that an official code/data repository does not exist globally. The tested arXiv article surface did not establish a released artifact that removes the model-execution and human-confirmation dependencies. Dataset-row-level reproduction was not attempted because the paper states the production ticket dataset cannot be released.
